traceability.notes:
The story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS defines an ESLint rule to enforce @story and @req annotations on significant control-flow branches, with requirements around branch detection, comment association, annotation parsing, configurable scope, nested/complex structures, performance, and documentation.
Based on the codebase: - Core functionality is implemented: the rule require-branch-annotation exists, uses helper utilities to detect configured branch node types, gathers associated comments, and checks for @story and @req, reporting and auto-fixing missing annotations. It supports many branch types (if/switch/loops/try/catch) and has logic to skip non-significant default switch cases. - Quality and integration standards are met at the design level: the rule follows ESLint RuleModule patterns, is registered in src/index.ts, and is included in recommended/strict configs. Helper functions are unit-tested, and RuleTester tests cover complex and nested branches, configurable branchTypes, and invalid configuration behavior. - User experience and error handling acceptance criteria appear satisfied at the implementation and test-specification level: the rule exposes a clear message "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.", offers auto-fixes for the first missing @story/@req per branch, and reports invalid configuration with descriptive messages listing allowed branch types. - Documentation exists and is linked to this story, giving usage, configuration, and examples, fulfilling the Documentation criterion.
However, the Definition of Done and acceptance criteria also require that tests are written and passing. When running Jest specifically against tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts via the project’s npm test script, the command exits with code 1. This indicates that the tests associated with this story either fail or trigger an error before completion. Without passing tests, we cannot confirm the rule’s behavior actually conforms to the specification in a verified way.
Therefore, despite a seemingly complete implementation, this story does not fully meet its own Definition of Done and acceptance criteria ("Tests written and passing"), and the correct assessment is FAILED.
